videos.title: Why the manual reading still wins
videos.summary: Where machines get blood pressure wrong, and why the cuff in your hands is the check the care team trusts.

videos.title: Know your kit, and zero the gauge
videos.summary: Every part of a manual blood pressure set, named and shown, ending with the zero check you do before you trust the dial.

videos.title: Find the brachial artery
videos.summary: Close-up of fingertips locating the pulse on the inner elbow, on three different arms.

videos.title: Set up the person, not just the cuff
videos.summary: Greeting, identity check, questions about coffee and smoking, five quiet minutes, and the seated position that protects the number.

videos.title: Arms you must not use
videos.summary: Dialysis access, IV lines, swelling, injury, and surgery on that side, and what to do when both arms are ruled out.

videos.title: Measure the arm, then pick the cuff
videos.summary: A tape measure at the mid-upper arm, the number read out loud, and the cuff chosen from the size chart.

videos.title: Wrong cuff, wrong number
videos.summary: The same arm measured three times with a small, a correct, and a large cuff, with the three readings side by side.

videos.title: Wrap it right
videos.summary: Artery marker on the artery, bottom edge an inch above the elbow crease, and the one-fingertip snugness test.

videos.title: Feel first, then pump
videos.summary: Feeling the wrist pulse while inflating, noting where it disappears, and pumping 30 above that point.

videos.title: The valve hand
videos.summary: A locked-off close-up of thumb and valve holding the needle at 2 to 4 mmHg per second, with a counter on screen.

videos.title: What the sounds really sound like
videos.summary: The Korotkoff phases played one at a time, loud and slow, so your ear learns the difference before it has to work at speed.

videos.title: Mark the first sound, mark the last
videos.summary: One measurement scored on screen, showing where a mark lands early, late, and on time.

videos.title: Read the dial, do not round it
videos.summary: Reading to the nearest 2 mmHg with your eye square to the dial, and how rounding to zeros hides real change.

videos.title: The silent gap, and other surprises
videos.summary: What an auscultatory gap does to a reading, plus faint sounds, sounds that never stop, and uneven beats.

videos.title: What the numbers mean
videos.summary: Adult categories, child percentiles, and the line between measuring a number and judging it.

videos.title: Say it out loud: reporting to the nurse
videos.summary: Three short handoffs, two done well and one done badly, so the shape of a good report is obvious.

videos.title: When not to trust your own reading
videos.summary: The four moments that should make you stop, wait, and measure again before you write anything down.

videos.title: Build the paper towel arm
videos.summary: Turning a roll of paper towels into a practice arm you can drill on tonight, for free.

videos.title: The whole skill, start to finish
videos.summary: One unbroken take of a complete manual blood pressure, from hand washing to charting, with nothing edited out.

videos.title: Read your own error pattern
videos.summary: Reading a practice history to tell a hand problem from an ear problem, and choosing what to drill next.
